content.text: I fixed it: both examples from the report now render as expected, and all tests pass. **Cause:** Before looking for emphasis (`**`, `*`, `_`, `~`), the lexer hides backslash-escaped characters so they can't count as delimiters. It did this before it recognised code spans. In `` `C:\Users\` `` the final `` \` `` was taken as an escaped backtick, so the code span wasn't found. The backticks then paired up wrongly, and `**home**` ended up treated as part of a code span. **Fix:** - `src/rules.ts`: I added a new pattern, `anyPunctuationOrCode`. It reads the text left to right and matches either a backslash escape, a whole code span, or an unclosed run of backticks. - `src/Lexer.ts`: the escape-hiding step now uses that pattern and only hides real escapes. Code spans and their backslashes are left as they are. The text stays the same length, which the later steps rely on. Escapes outside code spans work as before. For example, `` \`*a*` `` still gives `` `a` ``, and `\*a*` stays literal. **Tests:** I added `test/specs/new/code_span_trailing_backslash.md` and `.html`. They cover both examples from the report and a few nearby cases: an escaped backtick, an unclosed double-backtick run, an escape inside a code span within emphasis, and a literal `\*` followed by a code span. All 1911 spec tests and 199 unit tests pass, and the lint and type builds run cleanly. I didn't confirm that the new test fails on the old code, because the command that switched back to the old code needed an approval I didn't get.
